articles.title: USA DOE Closes $480MM Loan to Expand American Energy Output
articles.description: The U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Energy Dominance Financing announced the financial close of a $480 million loan for Arena Energy's Project Elkhorn.

articles.title: EIA Raises 2026, 2027 Oil Price Forecasts Yet Again
articles.description: The U.S. Energy Information Administration raised its 2026 and 2027 Brent oil spot price forecasts yet again in its latest short term energy outlook.

articles.title: Uniper Starts Green Hydrogen Production at Central German Energy Park
articles.description: Uniper and VNG H&V began producing renewable hydrogen at a 30-megawatt electrolysis plant at Energiepark Bad Lauchstadt, a federally funded project that developers describe as an industrial-scale laboratory for the entire hydrogen value chain.

articles.title: LNG is now the backbone of global gas trade, and the US is its biggest winner
articles.description: Geopolitical tensions are materially reshaping the global LNG landscape by tightening supply options and elevating price volatility across key consuming regions.

articles.title: Analyst Flags Oil's Biggest Threat
articles.description: Terri-Leigh Bennett, Chief Operating Officer of CMS Prime, flagged oil's biggest threat in an analysis piece sent to Rigzone.

articles.title: CNOOC discovers ultra-deep volcanic gas well in Bohai, China
articles.description: China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) has discovered an oil and gas well in ultra-deep volcanic formations in central Bohai, offshore China, more than 5,000m below the seabed.

articles.title: BASF opens $1bn MDI facility at Geismar site in Louisiana
articles.description: BASF, through its North American subsidiary, has inaugurated a new methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI) production facility at its Geismar Verbund site in Louisiana, US, following the completion of a $1bn investment project.

articles.title: Flex LNG Posts Record Q3 Revenue but Sees 'Muted' Spot Market Ahead
articles.description: Flex LNG logged $34.97 million in net profit adjusted for nonrecurring items for the third quarter, up from $23.52 million for the same three-month period last year as the LNG shipper posted its highest-ever revenue for the July-September period.

articles.title: Who is Really Paying for the Data Center Boom?
articles.description: The booming AI industry is consuming more and more power with each data center springing up across the United States. The surge in power demand necessitates grid upgrades and expansions in the energy infrastructure. But the costs are not allocated fairly, and households end up picking up the bill. Among residents, the costs are also disproportionately distributed, with the heaviest burden falling on rural and lower-income households, Cornell University researchers say. This week, Cornell researchers published a study in…

articles.title: Norway Regulator Widens Audit of AI Deployment in Oil Industry
articles.description: The Norwegian Ocean Industry Authority is reviewing how oil and gas companies vet artificial intelligence systems and manage risks from AI use in their workflows.

articles.title: EU Imports of Russian LNG Top 2025 Value Ahead of January Ban
articles.description: The EU has already paid more to import Russian LNG than it did for the whole of 2025, with a month and a half left until the full EU ban on imports of liquefied natural gas from Russia, German campaign group Urgewald said on Thursday. Between January and October, the EU paid as much as $9.6 billion (8.7 billion euros) to import gas from the Russian Yamal LNG project, according to Urgewald’s estimates based on vessel-tracking data by Kpler. The EU’s bill for importing Russian LNG has already topped by about 21% the estimated $8 billion…

articles.title: Gulf Overtakes Russia in Oil Sales to India
articles.description: Crude shipments reaching India through the crucial Middle East chokepoint have climbed to 2.1 million barrels a day so far this month, surpassing Russian imports of 1.8 million barrels a day, according to Kpler.

articles.title: Ukraine Peace Talks Yield Prisoner Deal but No Path to Peace
articles.description: The first trilateral negotiations between Russia, Ukraine, and the US since early this year produced a measured humanitarian breakthrough, but little tangible progress toward ending the war. The two days of talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10 -11 reached an agreement in principle on a large-scale prisoner exchange and opened discussions on broader European security arrangements. But the sides appear to be no closer to peace than they were 48 hours earlier. "The fundamental obstacle to ending this war is that neither belligerent currently sees an…

articles.title: Angola Looks to Diversify from Crude with Windfall Oil Revenues
articles.description: Angola has accelerated efforts to diversify its economy away from heavy dependence on oil by using this year’s windfall oil revenues to fund reforms and investments in transport corridors, minerals, banking, and tourism industries, according to Citigroup. “We’re definitely seeing a lot of activity and it has the benefit of longer-term political stability, economic stability, which is making it more attractive for foreign direct investment, infrastructure projects, and other longer-term investment,” Citi’s…

articles.title: Murphy Oil signs four production sharing contracts in Cameroon
articles.description: US-based Murphy Oil has signed four production sharing contracts covering approximately 2.6 million acres offshore Cameroon.

articles.title: Turkey Agrees to Record $1.6 Billion Climate Policy Funding Deal
articles.description: Turkey and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) on Thursday agreed on a $1.6-billion climate financing package to support Turkey’s climate goals in the biggest climate-focused deal of the Asian bank to date. The deal was announced in Antalya, where Turkey is hosting the COP31 global climate summit until November 20. Under the agreement, AIIB founding member Turkey will access a Climate-Focused Policy-Based Financing (CPBF) loan for the Türkiye Climate Action Acceleration Program (TCAAP) with supplemental…

articles.title: Nigeria Hits OPEC Oil Production Quota for Sixth Straight Month
articles.description: Nigeria’s crude oil output averaged 1.51 million barrels per day (bpd) in October as OPEC’s biggest African producer pumped to its quota for the sixth consecutive month, data from the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) showed this week. Nigeria last month pumped a total of 1.688 million barrels of crude oil and condensate per day, according to the data from its upstream regulator. Excluding condensate production, which is not part of the OPEC+ production quotas, Nigeria’s crude oil production alone averaged…

articles.title: India Boosts Gulf Oil Imports as Russian Crude Loses Its Price Advantage
articles.description: India has imported higher volumes of crude oil from the Persian Gulf than from Russia so far in November, for the first time since the Iran war broke out and disrupted the normal supply chain through the Strait of Hormuz. So far this month, India is estimated to have imported about 2.1 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil from the Persian Gulf, compared to 1.8 million bpd flows from Russia, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing data by Kpler. This is yet another sign that Strait of Hormuz flows have materially recovered in recent weeks,…

articles.title: China Targets Global Gas Turbine Market as AI Power Demand Explodes
articles.description: China is urging its gas turbine manufacturers to accelerate technology development and pitch sales to overseas data centers, the Chinese energy regulator said on Thursday, as Beijing targets challenging the Western firms’ dominance in this rapidly expanding market. Global orders for gas turbines have hit a record high as demand for power generation surges, JP Morgan said earlier this year. New gas turbine orders in the second quarter of the year stood at 38 gigawatts (GW), which was 29% higher than orders for the first quarter of the…

articles.title: Asian Oil Buyers Turn to Africa and Brazil as Tanker Rates Plunge
articles.description: Asian energy commodity buyers are increasingly turning to African and Brazilian grades, attracted by lower prices as rates for shipping oil out of the Persian Gulf remain near historic highs. Freight rates were at record levels for South American and African cargoes earlier this year, but have now declined enough to entice Asian buyers, Reuters noted in a report, citing unnamed sources including traders, shipbrokers, and analysts. The sources listed China’s Sinopec as one of these buyers along with South Korean SK Energy. Both companies bought…

articles.title: ASEAN Moves to Build Emergency Oil Reserves Amid Iran Supply Crisis
articles.description: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations has agreed to set up a joint crude oil stockpiling scheme in response to the supply disruption from the war in Iran, which severely affected countries in the region. The scheme will comprise storage sites in Indonesia and Thailand, Reuters reported today, from which ASEAN members will draw oil in times of tight supply. The withdrawals will be based on a ticket system, under which member countries would pay an advance fee to reserve the right to purchase a certain volume of oil or fuel from storage sites…

articles.title: Oil Prices Sink as Iran and Ukraine Peace Optimism Builds
articles.description: Crude oil prices extended their decline today, with both Brent crude and WTI shedding over $1 in Asian trade earlier in the day on growing hopes for peace in Ukraine and Iran. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $91.32 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate was changing hands for $85.32 per barrel. Peace hopes for Russia and Ukraine came on the heels of the latest meeting of negotiators, even though that meeting did not end in anything resembling a future peace deal. Besides yet another prisoner exchange, the two sides remain committed…

articles.title: Oil Rebounds Amid Mixed Iran War Signals
articles.description: Oil prices rose as uncertainty over the Iran war offset growing Persian Gulf supplies.

articles.title: Who Will Buy Sable’s Oil if California Keeps Closing Refineries?
articles.description: Situated off California’s Santa Barbara coast, the Santa Ynez project operated by Sable Offshore has become a litmus test of President Trump’s determination to revive oil production in a state pursuing a future beyond it. After a decade of shutdowns, its return depended on the Trump administration’s intervention in a prolonged regulatory battle. Originally developed by ExxonMobil, the Santa Ynez complex comprises the Hondo, Harmony and Heritage platforms and their associated onshore infrastructure. Its troubles began in May 2015,…
